## Purpose {.unnumbered .unlisted}

_How do we optimize datacenter efficiency and cost-per-goal for agentic workloads through test-time scaling, model routing, and post-training co-design?_

In classical serving, throughput is measured in tokens per second. In agentic serving, raw token throughput is a vanity metric: an agent burning 5,000 tokens/sec in an infinite loop has zero efficiency. The true macro-economic metric of autonomous computation is Trajectory Goodput: verified task outcomes per dollar per GPU-hour. Achieving high goodput requires navigating the Improvement Ladder: a strict economic hierarchy from prompt engineering to context working sets, tool ABIs, runtime verification gates, and trajectory distillation. By distilling successful MCTS search trajectories into base model weights via Reinforcement Learning on Verifiable Rewards (RLVR / GRPO), we compile runtime search scaffolding into compile-time model weights, shortening horizon $N$ and slashing serving costs. This chapter formalizes trajectory economics, heterogeneous SLM/LLM model routing, post-training co-design, and hardware co-design for CXL memory pooling.

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: _Maximizing raw token throughput (tokens/second) minimizes the operational cost of an agent cluster._

**Pitfall**: Ignoring the test-time compute Pareto frontier: spending 100 search steps on an underpowered model when a frontier model resolves the task in 2 steps.

:::

::: {.callout-takeaways title="Key Takeaways: Fleet Optimization"}

* **Trajectory Goodput:** Verified outcomes per dollar per GPU-hour is the true governing metric of agent serving.
* **The Improvement Ladder:** Systems optimization follows the Improvement Ladder: exhaust runtime scaffolding before retraining weights.
* **Heterogeneous cascades:** Routing tasks between small specialized models and frontier models minimizes serving cost.
* **Test-time compute amortization:** RLVR and trajectory distillation amortize expensive runtime search into compact model weights.

:::
